objects.title: The Orion Nebula
objects.subtitle: Messier 42
objects.what: A cloud of glowing gas where stars are being born right now. The four young stars at its heart, the Trapezium, light up the whole nebula.
facts: Neptune's whole orbit would cover a fifth of one pixel
objects.made: 39 frames of 20 s, with 16 of 2 s for the bright core
objects.how: 13 minutes of light on one field, plus short frames so the core does not burn out
specs: 39 x 20 s at ISO 3200 for the nebula; 16 x 2 s at ISO 800 for the core
69 long frames taken, 39 kept. 30 lost to passing cloud (stars dimmed to between 3 and 77 percent)
The 2 s stack replaces the 20 s stack wherever any frame came within 7 percent of clipping: 31 star cores, the Trapezium among them. Measured ratio 41.0, expected 40
0.776 arcsec per pixel: one pixel per 2 x 2 colour cell. Stars 4.2 arcsec wide
4 October 2026, before dawn. 41 to 46 degrees up, 41 percent Moon in the sky, thin cloud passing
Flat from 26 twilight-sky frames, its large-scale shape from cloud-lit frames. No darks
RAW colour planes (no demosaic), hot pixels by 3 x 3 median, registered on stars with rotation, sigma-clipped mean. One sky constant per colour
Black 19 and white 217 of 255, gamma 0.95, S-curve 0.3. Saturation x 1.6 in CIELAB. Dark sky made neutral and smoothed (bilateral, 2.5 px)

objects.title: The Moon at last quarter

objects.what: Along the line between day and night the Sun is setting, so every crater rim and mountain throws a long shadow. That is why the detail is richest there.
facts: 365,000 km, measured from its size in this picture
Copernicus is 93 km wide; Clavius, 231 km

specs: 78 taken over five aims in two passes, 39 kept. 17 saw only the night side; the rest were lost to cloud
Frames registered on the lunar surface itself (12,000 matched features, 0.8 px). In each patch only the sharpest 30 percent of the clear frames are averaged

0.388 arcsec per pixel, the sensor's own: 0.7 km per pixel on the Moon

specs: 10 s at ISO 1600, about 7 frames per panel: one minute each
72 taken, 60 kept: 10 minutes in all. Panels 3 and 7 were shot through cloud and only fill where clear panels have no data

1.553 arcsec per pixel. Stars about 5 arcsec wide; the bright ones are saturated and left white
99 x 63 arcmin, cropped level from the mosaic; one frame is 38.8 x 25.8

facts: 2.5 million years ago, when our ancestors were first making stone tools
Each pixel is about 10 light-years across
objects.how: An hour on one field; cloud took two frames in three

4 October 2026, after midnight, over 70 minutes. 83 degrees up, Moon just rising

Flat built from the clouded frames themselves: cloud glow seen through the optics, less the scaled clear frame. Dust shadows left out of the average. No darks

objects.title: Saturn and seven of its moons
objects.subtitle: At opposition, 4 October 2026
objects.what: Saturn at its closest and brightest for the year, its rings tilted only a few degrees toward us. Every labelled point is a moon. Titan, the big one, is larger than the planet Mercury.
facts: 270,000 km tip to tip: 70 percent of the way from Earth to the Moon
The three inner moons are named from how they moved between frames
objects.made: Planet: the 16 sharpest of 48 frames at 1/40 s; moons: 2 s frames
objects.how: Two exposures in one picture: 1/40 s for the planet, 2 s for the moons
specs: Planet: 1/40 s at ISO 800. Moons: 2 s at ISO 6400, 640 times the planet's exposure
Planet: 61 taken, 48 usable, the 16 sharpest kept. Moons: 2 clear frames; the other ten were behind cloud

Each RAW colour plane placed at its own sub-pixel offset on a grid 3 x finer than the sensor (0.129 arcsec). No demosaic. Colours re-registered for the air's prism effect. Shown here at the sensor's scale, not enlarged
Blur measured from Titan in the same frames: 2.7 x 2.2 arcsec (5.0 x 4.0 before the refocus). Richardson-Lucy, 8 rounds; stopped where a model planet starts to grow a false rim
The planet is set into the moon field where the 2 s frames are blown out. The planet's glare is subtracted ring by ring. Moons are lifted about 640 x relative to the planet
Field: 0.388 arcsec per pixel, north up (9 catalogue stars, 0.6 arcsec)
4 October 2026, after midnight, over 19 minutes. 52 degrees up, at opposition
No ephemeris used: each point keeps its place beside Saturn while the stars slide past, and sits at its orbit's reach. Worth a check
The Cassini division: no dip along the ring line in the plain stack or the restored one
